subject: Urgent: checkout latency spikes + error burst (possible SDK stream parser issue)
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@edgecommerce.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Julian Park <julian@edgecommerce.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in checkout latency & errors today

Hi Tessa,

We started seeing a sudden spike in checkout latency and 5xx errors around 08:50 PDT. P99 has jumped to ~6s and our checkout failures increased by ~3% in a 12-minute window. We pushed the latest Redwood client SDK (v2.7.1) a week ago and are wondering if this is related.

Attached are a short slice of request IDs and the NDJSON we captured from our edge for 08:45-09:00. We're flagged a handful of sessions where the client appears to resend the same streaming frames; in our logs we see repeated header blocks and then an abrupt connection reset.

This is impacting a subset of EU customers routing through our US region — high priority for us. Can you confirm whether this matches any known SDK issues and if you can triage immediately?

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Integrations, EdgeCommerce

Attachments: edgecommerce_error_log_0601.ndjson

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Spike in checkout latency & errors today

Immediate asks:
- Irene/Sean: can you confirm whether repeated header blocks / "double-CRLF" observed in NDJSON map to any parser edge-case in client SDK v2.7.1?

Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@edgecommerce.com>, Julian Park <julian@edgecommerce.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in checkout latency & errors today

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Replayed the NDJSON slice. Observed a pattern where incoming stream chunks occasionally contain an extra CRLF sequence between token frames when the client is under bursty retransmit. The streaming parser in the v2.x client SDK treats this as a boundary and attempts to reparse headers, leading to a small synchronous reassembly path which increases p99 and can produce a 400-level parsing error when the buffer aligns badly.
- Root cause hypothesis: a race in the client's write path that causes header coalescence + an extra CRLF during high retry bursts. This manifests as both latency (parser stalls on unexpected boundary) and an uptick in parse errors that bubble up as 5xx on your side.
- Repro: consistent when replayed at ~300 concurrent streams in our local harness. Not seen in v1.x legacy client.

Mitigation plan (short-term):
1) Recommend EdgeCommerce enable a temporary rate-limit window (burst smoothing) for sessions routing to Redwood for the next 2 hours — reduces occurrence while we ship a fix.
2) We'll prepare a server-side tolerant fallback that ignores spurious CRLF-only boundaries for the next 24–48 hours (rollout target: canary within 3 hours).
3) Engineering will prepare a v2.7.2 patch to make the client parser robust to stray CRLFs and improve buffering (hotfix candidate).

I’m attaching a short SDK trace showing the parser state transitions (sdk_dump_trace.txt) and a bisect diff we’re using to confirm the minimal change (hotfix_bisect.diff).

I'll follow up with a canary rollout plan and ETA for the client patch.

—Irene
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sdk_dump_trace.txt, hotfix_bisect.diff

From: Sara Patel <sara@edgecommerce.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in checkout latency & errors today

Thanks Irene — we can enable a short burst-smoothing rule from 11:15–13:15 PDT and will route a sample test swarm at 11:30 to validate. Sample request-id: req_20280601_2312. SDK user-agent string: RedwoodJS/2.7.1 (+EdgeCommerce-integration/1.4.0).

We need ETA on safe rollback or hotfix timeline — our ops and execs are watching conversions. If you think a server-side tolerant fallback buys us time, we’ll accept that now. Please advise ASAP.

—Sara

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary: EdgeCommerce checkout impact (requested credit & SLA exception)

Vivek — heads up. EdgeCommerce experienced a revenue-impacting degradation this morning due to what appears to be a client SDK parser edge-case when under bursty retries (details below). They’ve asked for an SLA exception window and a partial credit if we can’t fully mitigate within the next 24 hours.

Quick facts: ~3% checkout failure delta for ~12 minutes, P99 up ~4–5s during the burst. We have a clear repro and an actionable mitigation (server-side tolerant fallback + quick client hotfix). Engineering expects a canary of the fallback in ~3 hours and a client patch candidate in the next 6–8 hours.

Recommend we approve the rolling fallback and prepare a goodwill credit offer if the client still sees >1% delta after rollouts. I’ll coordinate comms if you approve.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in checkout latency & errors today — next steps and ETA

Sara — short update and next steps: 
- We’ll roll a server-side tolerant fallback into the canary pool at 16:00 PDT (ETA 35 minutes). This change is aimed at ignoring stray CRLF-only boundaries so your flows don’t trigger the expensive reassembly path.
- Engineering will publish a v2.7.2 client patch today; tentative release time 19:00 PDT with a coordinated canary. We recommend upgrading but it’s not immediately required if you accept the server fallback while we validate.
- Marissa has flagged the exec ask for credit/SLA exception; we’ll keep you posted — our goal is to avoid customer impact and minimize credits.

I’ll follow up with the canary results at ~17:00 PDT. Appreciate the quick logs — they were critical to root causing this one.

Best,
Tessa
